name: agent-farm
description: Mission control for your local coding agents — Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Antigravity and OpenCode: live fleet status, cost analytics, session explorer, health & optimization insights.

walkthroughs.title: Agent Farm: Setup in Five Steps
walkthroughs.description: From live monitoring to your first autonomous job — mission control for your agent fleet.

steps.title: 1 · Introduce your agents
steps.description:
Agent Farm treats every folder with a CLAUDE.md under your root folders as an agent.
[Add Agent Root](command:agentfarm.addAgentRoot)

steps.title: 2 · Install the live hooks
steps.description:
Hooks forward every agent event (prompt, tool, permission wait) to the local listener — the timeline and notifications run on them.
[Install Live Hooks](command:agentfarm.installHooks)

steps.title: 3 · Open the Dashboard
steps.description:
Costs, health and the Farm Status card — which subsystem is dormant, at a glance.
[Open Dashboard](command:agentfarm.openDashboard)

steps.title: 4 · Set up your first automation
steps.description:
A working example in one click: an inbox duty, a morning briefing or a two-agent chain.
[Set Up Example Automation](command:agentfarm.setupExample)

steps.title: 5 · Explore the guide
steps.description:
The built-in guide (English by default, Türkçe selectable; 25 scenarios): media pipeline, webhook bridge, multi-agent chains…
[Open Guide](command:agentfarm.openGuide)

enumDescriptions: English
Türkçe
agentFarm.guideLanguage.description: Language of the in-app help: the Guide, Quick Start and Examples. It can also be switched from the language toggle inside the guide panel.

enumDescriptions: Follow VS Code's display language (English where there is no translation); dates and numbers keep your system's formats
English
Türkçe
agentFarm.language.description: Language of the Agent Farm pages. Translations are added one surface at a time; anything not translated yet is shown in English. Choosing a language also formats dates and times in it. Pages pick up a change the next time they are drawn (Refresh or reopen).

agentFarm.agentRoots.description: Root folders scanned for agent directories. Subfolders containing CLAUDE.md, .claude or memory/ become agents. A root whose subfolders are agents is a nest — its own CLAUDE.md counts as shared instructions, not an agent; a root with no agent-like subfolders is one agent itself. Manage this comfortably in the Agent folders section of Farm Settings.

agentFarm.excludeAgentDirs.description: Folders that are never treated as agents, even when they look like one. Compared case- and slash-insensitively. Easiest managed via Exclude/Include in the Agent folders section of Farm Settings.

agentFarm.newAgentModel.description: Default model written into a new agent's .claude/settings.local.json when the agent is created via Agent Farm — an alias (haiku, sonnet, opus, fable) or a full model id. Empty = write no model, the Claude CLI default applies. Existing agents' models are managed per agent in the Agent folders section of Farm Settings.

agentFarm.modelAliases.description: The model names offered in every model picker (Agent folders, missions, the Start Session launcher). Add a new name here once and it is offered everywhere; every picker also takes a name typed by hand.

agentFarm.web.enabled.markdownDescription: Serve a read-only web view of the farm, the same figures the panel shows, sized for a phone. While VS Code is closed the background service keeps serving the last snapshot and says so. It answers this machine only unless Reachable from says else, a token is always required, and nothing on it can change anything. Open Web View gives the address.

agentFarm.web.port.description: The port the read-only web view listens on; it must differ from Listener port.

enumDescriptions: Only this machine (127.0.0.1).
Your network: your phone or a second machine can reach it.
agentFarm.web.bind.markdownDescription: This machine only (127.0.0.1), or your network too, so your phone or a second machine can reach it. Network reach is opt-in on purpose; the token stays required either way and the view stays read-only.

agentFarm.web.token.description: Access token for the web view. Generated for you the first time you enable it; anyone with this token can READ the farm's dashboard, so treat it like a password. Empty = the server refuses to start.

enumDescriptions: No phone can reach this farm.
Only this machine (127.0.0.1) — for testing with an emulator.
Your home or office network: the pairing QR names this machine's private addresses.
Your Tailscale network: listens on this machine's 100.x address only.
agentFarm.remote.listen.markdownDescription: Where the Agent Farm phone app can reach this farm. Off by default. Every connection is TLS with a certificate the phone pins at pairing, and every phone is paired once with a QR code and can be revoked at any time. Only the window that runs the task queue listens.

agentFarm.remote.port.description: Port the phone app connects to (TLS). Must differ from the web view and live-hook ports.

agentFarm.telegram.enabled.markdownDescription: Let a Telegram chat talk to your agents: the agent the chat is bound to runs each message and answers in the same thread. The bot token lives in Secrets; set it up with Connect Telegram. A chat not in Allowed chats is refused and told its id; chat-started runs stop at Daily remote budget. Commands: /agent, /new, /agents, /status, /cancel, /help.

agentFarm.telegram.allowedChats.description: Telegram chat ids allowed to drive the farm. EMPTY = nobody can (the bridge answers every message with a refusal and its own chat id). This is the access list for something that spends money — keep it to your own chats.

agentFarm.telegram.maxDailyUSD.description: Ceiling on what remote work may cost per day (API-equivalent), shared by Telegram and the Agent Farm phone app: one total, whichever spent it. Past it a new run from chat is refused and a message into a live conversation asks for a yes first. 0 = every remote message asks and no run starts from chat; commands like /status keep working.

agentFarm.telegram.defaultAgent.description: Agent a new chat talks to before it picks one with /agent. Empty = a chat must bind an agent first.

enumDescriptions: A chat hears the turn cards of the conversation it is focused on (/focus), or of the only live one — where a reply from it would go.
Every allowed chat hears every live conversation's turn cards.
No turn cards; commands and replies keep working.
agentFarm.telegram.digest.markdownDescription: When a Console turn ends, or an agent stops to ask you something, the chat gets a card: what the agent said, what it waits on and what the turn cost, with buttons (a question's options, Allow / Deny, Continue, Cancel, Diff, Status).

enumDescriptions: The message waits and goes in as the next turn's first words, and the chat is told so. Survives a window reload.
The message goes into the turn that is running, where the engine allows it — the same steering the Console composer does.
agentFarm.telegram.whenBusy.markdownDescription: What a message from a chat meets when the agent is already working. Wait parks it and sends it in when the turn ends, since from a phone you cannot see what the agent is doing. Steer sends it into the running turn on engines that allow it (Claude); the others wait anyway.

agentFarm.a2a.preferredGraceHours.markdownDescription: How long an agent-to-agent note or task marked preferred is its target role's alone. After that, anyone in the same project with the required skills may read or claim it, ranked below an exact fit. 0 opens it at once. A hard note never opens; an any note never waits.

agentFarm.accounts.markdownDescription: The engine sign-ins captured on this machine. An account is its own config folder: a session started with it points the engine there (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for Claude Code), so two accounts can run at once. Capture one on the Engines page after signing in normally. No token is stored here.

id.description: Folder-safe id, minted from the address.

engine.description: Which engine this sign-in belongs to. An account belongs to one engine.

label.description: What you call it. The address is the fallback.

dir.description: The config directory this account IS.

email.description: The address this sign-in belongs to, read off the disk when it was captured. Empty is normal on engines that do not record one.

subscriptionType.description: The plan the sign-in states (pro, max, chatgpt...). What the account is entitled to is between you and the vendor; this is only what the file said.

capturedAt.description: When it was sealed, epoch ms.

agentFarm.activeAccounts.markdownDescription: Which account the next session on each engine uses, by engine id, set with "Use this next" on the Engines page. Empty = the main sign-in, exactly as without accounts.

agentFarm.providerProfiles.markdownDescription: The routes Agent Farm holds: provider, endpoint and the model each tier resolves to; one route can serve Claude Code, OpenCode or both. Managed on the Engines page › Providers. No key is ever written here: it is kept in the OS keychain under the route's id, and anything typed here that is not a route field is dropped.

id.description: Permanent handle, 2–40 characters of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It is also the key the credential is stored under, so it cannot contain a dot, a space or a slash — and it cannot be changed. Copy the profile to a new id instead (the copy starts with no key).

label.description: What a picker shows. Free to change at any time; renaming does not bump the revision, because the revision is a statement about the route rather than a count of edits.

engines.description: The engines this route serves: claude, opencode or both. Every one marked must be able to run it — OpenCode needs an endpoint and at least one tier. Left out, the route serves every engine it can.

providerId.description: Which provider this routes to — anthropic, anthropic-api, kimi, minimax, or one you describe yourself.

baseUrl.description: The Anthropic-compatible endpoint Claude Code is pointed at. Empty = first-party. Must be https, or http on this machine (localhost / 127.0.0.1): a key sent over plain http to another host travels in clear. Never ends in /v1: Claude Code adds /v1/messages itself.

opencodeUrl.description: Where OpenCode reaches this service in the OpenAI style, when that is not the endpoint above. A route with only this serves OpenCode alone. The same https rule applies.

authKind.description: Which header carries the key: api-key sends x-api-key, oauth sends Authorization: Bearer.

context.description: The context window of the route's models, in tokens.

output.description: The longest answer the route's models give, in tokens.

tiers.description: tier → model id: which model this route serves for opus / sonnet / haiku. Empty = the route's own defaults.

revision.description: Managed by Agent Farm. Starts at 1 and only ever counts up.

engine.description: Which engine every new session, task and automation starts on. Empty = Claude Code, which is what every launch meant before engines existed. ‼️ A per-turn engine such as Codex or Antigravity behaves differently: a message typed mid-turn is HELD until the turn ends, the model/effort/permission pickers are the NEXT turn's flags, and it reports tokens rather than a price because it runs against a plan. On Codex the permission mode becomes a sandbox chosen up front (it cannot stop and ask); on Antigravity ('agy') the real restraint is the Antigravity app's own tool-permission setting rather than this one, and it only sees folders it is explicitly given. 'agy' is Antigravity, Google's agent app — NOT the separate 'gemini' CLI above it. An engine that is not installed or not signed in on this machine is refused at start — see Agent Farm: Open Engines.

model.description: --model for every session (alias or full id). Empty = the agent's own setting / the CLI default.

effort.description: --effort for every session. Empty = no flag.

permissionMode.description: --permission-mode for every session. Empty = no flag (asks, as configured).

agentFarm.launchDefaults.markdownDescription: How **every** interactive session starts: Start, Continue and Resume, from the tree, the palette or a key. Each field is optional and an empty one adds no flag, so `{}` starts the bare `claude`. The **Start Session…** launcher shows these as inherited values and can override them once or save itself back here.

agentFarm.flexOverrides.markdownDescription: Preference values set for one agent or one project: `{ "agent": { "developer": { "retry.supervisor.engine": "codex" } }, "project": { "prj_x": { … } } }`. A project's value beats the agent's, the agent's beats Farm Settings, and a workflow, step or run beats them all. Agents by name, projects by id. Set with `flex.set`.

agentFarm.flexPresets.markdownDescription: Your own presets: a named set of preference values (flex points) applied together. The built-in ones — Economy · Balanced · Quality — are not stored here. Apply one with `presets.apply`; editing a value afterwards never changes the preset.

values.description: Flex point id → value, e.g. {"retry.supervisor.maxCalls": 1}. flex.list names every point.

scope.description: global = everywhere; project = only in the project named below.

project.description: The project id, for a project preset.

describe.description: One line on what it is for.

family.description: Presets that are alternatives to each other share a family (cost, …).

name.description: profile name shown in the launcher

agentId.description: the agent this setup starts when pressed on the Start Session… icon (written by Save in the launcher); leave it out and that press asks which agent

engine.description: which engine the session runs on; leave it out for the default engine

providerId.description: which route the session runs on: a stored route on Claude, the engine's own provider on OpenCode

tier.description: which tier of that route (Claude, only together with a route)

account.description: which sign-in of that engine the setup opens on; a sign-in no longer on this machine arrives empty

variant.description: the model's reasoning variant, where the engine offers one

superpowers.description: start under the engineering-discipline skills (true) or without them (false); leave it out and the agent's own default decides

surface.description: where the session opens; leave it out and the launcher keeps the surface it is on

prompt.description: optional first prompt sent with the session

agentFarm.launchProfiles.markdownDescription: Saved launch setups offered by the **Start Session…** launcher — "deep review" (opus + xhigh + plan), "quick fix" (sonnet + acceptEdits), and so on. The launcher's *Save this as a profile…* row writes here; nothing is applied until you pick one.

agentFarm.console.autoAnswer.enabled.markdownDescription: When a **Console** question waits longer than "Answer after", the option the agent marked **(Recommended)**, or its first, is chosen so an unattended session is not held for ever. The card counts down and has **Stop timer**. Never for a permission request, a question with no options or one that reads as destructive.

agentFarm.console.autoAnswer.timeoutSeco.markdownDescription: How long a **Console** question waits for you before the recommended option is chosen, counted from when it was asked; reopening the window does not restart it. Values outside 5–7200 are clamped, and a change re-arms questions already waiting.

agentFarm.console.autoAnswer.remindSecon.markdownDescription: How long before a **Console** question answers itself its reminder rings: the tone and, with Say who on for Asking you, a sentence naming whose question it is. Once per question. Mute all and quiet hours hold it; a session set to Silent does not. `0` = off.

enumDescriptions: No filter: the clock runs on every question and the recommended option is chosen — only your own Stop timer on the card halts it.
Read only the question and the option the clock would choose (default): a word in another option's description does not stop it.
Read the question and every option and description: any listed word anywhere stops the clock.
As 'all', and a question that marks no option "(Recommended)" also waits for you.
agentFarm.console.autoAnswer.filter.markdownDescription: Which **Console** questions the timer leaves for you because they carry a hold-back word: `recommended` reads the question and the option it would choose, `all` every option, `strict` also waits when no option is recommended, `off` holds nothing back.

agentFarm.console.autoAnswer.words.markdownDescription: Words that make a **Console** question wait for you instead of being answered on the timer. Each matches at the start of a word, any case (`delet` catches `deleted`); an entry written `/…/` is a regular expression. An empty list holds nothing back. How much of a question is read: "What holds a question back".

agentFarm.notifyConsoleTurnEnd.markdownDescription: The **"‹agent› is waiting for you"** box in VS Code's corner when a **Console** turn ends and you are not watching it, with a button that opens it. Never for the session on screen or a turn you interrupted. The Notices reminder of the same name is "Idle session reminder"; the Console's own signals do not depend on this.

agentFarm.speakerLabelTemplate.markdownDescription: How the AI is labelled in transcripts (Turns, Session Viewer and their Markdown exports), built from each message's model: `{ai}` the engine, `{model}` the family, `{version}` the version, `{raw}` the model id. Other text is kept as written, so `MyBot` is a fixed label. Empty = `{ai}`. Its case is "Speaker label case".

enumDescriptions: Match the page — Session Viewer upper (like USER), Turns lower (like user/tool). The current default.
Force UPPER CASE everywhere
Force lower case everywhere
As-is — leave the template's own case untouched (use for a fixed brand label)
agentFarm.speakerLabelCase.description: The letter case of the AI speaker label: as the page writes its other speakers, upper, lower, or exactly as the template writes it.

agentFarm.speakerLabelFallback.description: AI speaker label shown when the model id yields nothing to fill the template (unknown engine, <synthetic>, or missing). Never 'assistant' — this is an agent.

agentFarm.claudeDir.description: Path to the Claude Code data directory. Leave empty to use ~/.claude.

name.description: Machine label shown on sessions (e.g. laptop)

dir.description: Path to that machine's synced .claude folder

agentFarm.extraClaudeDirs.description: Additional (read-only, synced) Claude data folders from other machines — e.g. a Syncthing/OneDrive copy of the laptop's ~/.claude. Their sessions appear with a ⇄ machine badge.

agentFarm.activeThresholdSeconds.description: A session is considered ACTIVE if its transcript changed within this many seconds.

agentFarm.staleMemoryDays.description: Memory files untouched for more than this many days are flagged as stale.

agentFarm.contextBudgetTokens.description: Warn when an agent's fixed context load (CLAUDE.md + MEMORY.md + AGENTS.md) exceeds this estimated token budget.

agentFarm.forecastDays.description: How many days ahead the Task Forecast projects scheduled runs.

agentFarm.windowTokenLimit.description: Optional token limit for the rolling 5-hour usage window (subscription plans). 0 hides the progress bar and shows raw totals.

enumDescriptions: Weigh the kinds of token AND the model: one Sonnet input token = 1, Opus = 5, Haiku = 1/3. The default — a haiku test must not read as expensive as opus work.
Weigh only the KINDS of token (output x5, 1h cache-write x2, 5m cache-write x1.25, cache-read x0.1) and ignore which model ran.
Turn the weighting off: the ⚖ figure becomes the raw total.
agentFarm.quotaWeightMode.description: How the weighted figure, what work costs the plan's rolling limit rather than how many tokens moved, is worked out. By default both the kind of token and the model count, so a Haiku test does not read as costly as Opus work.

agentFarm.quotaWeights.description: Override the weight table behind the weighted figure; empty = the built-in one. Each rule matches a model id and weighs input, output, cache writes (5-minute and 1-hour) and cache reads against one Sonnet input token = 1. The first rule that matches wins; an unmatched model counts as Sonnet, never as zero. Kept apart from Model prices.

match.description: Regex matched against the model id (case-insensitive).

input.description: Weight of one fresh input token.

output.description: Weight of one output token — thinking is billed here too, and it is the biggest spender in a turn.

cacheWrite1h.description: Weight of one 1-hour-TTL cache-creation token — the rate that actually applies on this machine.

cacheRead.description: Weight of one cache-read token. This is 94-99% of any raw total, which is why the raw figure says so little about the limit.

enumDescriptions: Brake on whichever ceiling is further along — the safe default when both are configured.
Brake only on the ⚖ weighted figure against windowWeightedTokenLimit.
Brake only on the raw total against windowTokenLimit — how it behaved before the weighted figure existed.
agentFarm.quotaBrakeBasis.description: Which figure Hold starts at and Downgrade at read to judge how full the five-hour window is. A limit that is not set is never read, whatever this says; set Window limit or Weighted window limit first.

agentFarm.windowWeightedTokenLimit.description: The rolling five-hour limit in weighted tokens instead of raw ones. Set it to what your plan really allows (watch the weighted figure in a window where you hit the limit); the start brake and the model downgrade then read it. 0 = off. With both limits set, Brake on decides which one counts.

agentFarm.planUsageRefreshMinutes.description: How often your Claude plan limits are re-read while no agent is mid-turn; while one is, Refresh while working takes over. One read serves the status-bar indicator, the Dashboard's Plan usage card and the bridge. 0 turns automatic refresh off in both cases; Check now and the card's refresh button still work.

agentFarm.planUsageActiveRefreshSeconds.description: How often the same figures are re-read while an agent is mid-turn, when they really move; a turn starting or ending also reads once. Minimum 30 seconds: the endpoint answers a faster poller with a persistent HTTP 429, met by an automatic backoff that one success clears. Ignored while Refresh while idle is 0.

agentFarm.agyUsageRefreshMinutes.description: How often Antigravity's quota is re-read while no Antigravity turn runs. Each read runs agy -p /usage in the background (no tokens), which briefly flashes a terminal. Other engines' turns (Claude, Codex…) do not count. It is also read when the window opens and after each Antigravity run. 0 = only those reads and Check now.

agentFarm.agyUsageActiveRefreshSeconds.description: How often Antigravity's quota is re-read while an Antigravity turn runs, counted from the run's start. Claude or Codex working does not switch it on. Minimum 30 seconds.

agentFarm.planUsageMinIntervalSeconds.description: The shortest gap between two usage requests for one sign-in, across everything that reads it (background, status bar, turn ends, account cards, bridge). A read that comes too early gets the figure taken moments ago instead. Raise it if an account still gets rate limited; the floor is 5 seconds. It never causes an extra read.

agentFarm.planUsageStatusBar.description: Keep your plan's session countdown and usage in the VS Code status bar, e.g. 3h 49m - 86% / wk 41%: time left in this session window, how much of it is used, and how much of the week. Hover for every limit and its reset time; click for the Dashboard card. Hidden on a machine with no Claude subscription sign-in.

agentFarm.accountsAutoRefresh.description: Re-read every captured sign-in's window figures in the background, page open or not, each on its own beat (Refresh while working during a turn, Refresh while idle otherwise) and never all at once. Off costs nothing: a card's refresh, Refresh all and the turn-end read still work. The Engines page's Auto-refresh button flips it too.

enumDescriptions: Claude Code — read from Anthropic's own usage endpoint, refreshed on the beat below.
Codex — read from its own transcript, which records the limit the service returned on its last turn. Free, but as old as that turn.
Gemini — billed per token against an API key: there is no plan window, so the indicator says so instead of showing a bar.
Antigravity — publishes no quota figure this machine can read; the indicator says so rather than showing 0%.
OpenCode — each model runs against its own provider, so there is no single plan window; it states the price of every turn instead.
agentFarm.planUsageEngine.description: Which engine's remaining limit the status bar shows. Hover the indicator to see them all and switch, or use the tabs on the Dashboard's Plan usage card; both write this setting.

agentFarm.planUsageWarnPercent.description: The status-bar usage indicator turns yellow once any of your plan's limits reaches this percentage.

agentFarm.planUsageDangerPercent.description: The status-bar figure turns red here; 101 = never.

agentFarm.maxTranscriptMessages.description: Maximum number of messages rendered in the session viewer.

agentFarm.contextWindowTokens.description: The context window every "Context now" figure and the handover thresholds are measured against. 0 = the engine's own window (Codex reports one per turn), else the Context of the session's route, else the model's known one; with none, the raw token count shows with no percent.

agentFarm.contextConvergePct.description: When a running session's context window is this full, it is told once (CONTEXT CONVERGE) to start nothing new and finish the step in flight. On an engine whose hooks cannot carry the message, the crossing is recorded as undelivered. 0 = off.

agentFarm.contextHandoverPct.description: When a running session's context window is this full, it is told once (CONTEXT HANDOVER) to stop, commit, write its handover note and end the run. A converge line above it is folded down onto it. 0 = off.

agentFarm.quotaConvergePct.description: When the five-hour window of the account a running session is signed in as is this full, it is told once (QUOTA CONVERGE) to start nothing new. Off by default: below the handover line a run works at full capacity. Read from the session's own sign-in; a session whose sign-in is unknown is not told. 0 = off.

agentFarm.quotaHandoverPct.description: When the five-hour window of the session's own account is this full, it is told once (QUOTA HANDOVER) to stop, commit, write its handover note and end the run. A converge line above it is folded down onto it. 0 = off.

agentFarm.quotaWeeklyHandoverPct.description: When the session's own account has used this much of its weekly window, it is told once (QUOTA HANDOVER, naming the week) to stop, commit, write its handover note or pass the baton, and end the run; a relay's next leg never stays on that account. Each window has its own line, said once until it turns over. 0 = off.

agentFarm.disciplineOrders.description: What the converge and handover warnings order a running session to do. The lead words and the reading before them are fixed; this is the instruction that follows. A run in a baton relay has its own branches, told to pass the baton instead of writing a note. Leave a field empty for its built-in sentence; {chain} becomes the relay's chain and leg.

converge.default: Start nothing new — no new sub-task, no broad reads — finish the atomic step in flight, then hand over (_REF/handover.md).
converge.description: The converge line, outside a relay: the run may still work but starts nothing new.

handover.default: Stop here: finish nothing further, commit the clean progress, write the handover note and end the run — the next run continues from the note (_REF/handover.md).
handover.description: The handover line, outside a relay: stop, commit, write the note, end the run.

relayConverge.default: Start nothing new — no new sub-task, no broad reads — finish the atomic step in flight, then pass the baton ({chain}; _REF/handover.md).
relayConverge.description: The converge line for a run inside a baton relay — it ends by passing the baton, not by writing a note.

relayHandover.default: You run in a {chain}: stop here, finish nothing further, commit the clean progress and pass the baton instead of writing a handover note — Write { "prompt": "<what your successor starts from>" } to a file, run node af.js baton.pass "@<file>", then end the run; the next runner opens once this session has ended (_REF/handover.md).
relayHandover.description: The handover line for a run inside a baton relay: the successor's first message IS the handover, so this names the command that writes it.

relayPassedConverge.default: Your baton is already passed ({chain}): start nothing new, finish the step in flight and end the run — the successor opens once this session has ended (_REF/handover.md).
relayPassedConverge.description: The converge line for a relay runner that has ALREADY passed its baton — there is nothing left to hand over, only to end.

relayPassedHandover.default: Your baton is already passed ({chain}): commit anything left and end the run now — the successor opens once this session has ended (_REF/handover.md).
relayPassedHandover.description: The handover line for a relay runner that has already passed its baton: commit and end, the successor is waiting on this session.

relayBrakedConverge.default: The user braked your {chain} — this is its LAST leg: start nothing new — no new sub-task, no broad reads — finish the atomic step in flight, then write the handover note instead of passing the baton (_REF/handover.md).
relayBrakedConverge.description: The converge line for a relay leg the user braked as the chain's last (the brake on its Console card, or baton.lastLeg): it ends with the handover note, not a pass.

relayBrakedHandover.default: The user braked your {chain} — this is its LAST leg, so do NOT call baton.pass: stop here, finish nothing further, commit the clean progress, write the handover note (_REF/handover.md, section 4) and end the run — no successor opens; a person continues from the note.
relayBrakedHandover.description: The handover line for a relay leg the user braked as the chain's last: no successor opens, so it names the note, as outside a relay.

agentFarm.batonMaxHops.description: The most legs one relay chain may run; the run that started it is leg 1. A pass from the last leg opens nothing: the baton is kept as stopped, the runner writes a handover note instead, and Notices says so once. Two legs in a row ending on the same commit stop the chain too. 0 = no ceiling.

agentFarm.batonInjectedDirective.description: A standing rule said to every leg of every chain, above the predecessor's own words, e.g. run npm test before you pass the baton. Empty = nothing is added. In your own leg message template it goes where {userDirective} stands, or on its own line if the template does not name it.

agentFarm.batonHandoverTemplate.description: Your own first message for every leg, in place of the built-in header. Variables: {leg} (this leg), {hop} (passes so far), {maxHops}, {chain}, {agentId}, {fromSessionId} (the predecessor), {why}, {userDirective}, {agentPrompt} (the predecessor's words), {relayRules}. A template without the last two still gets them. Empty = the built-in header.

agentFarm.batonEmergencyTemplate.description: Your own first message for a leg the failsafe opens after a cut-off leg (told to hand over, an error, uncommitted work). Variables: {leg}, {hop}, {maxHops}, {chain}, {agentId}, {fromSessionId}, {why}, {evidence} (what it left), {userDirective}, {relayRules}; without {evidence} a template gets it, last. Empty = the built-in header.

agentFarm.batonFaultWaitHours.description: When a leg's turn fails because the engine is down, overloaded, unreachable, rate limited or refuses the sign-in, no new leg is opened; the same session is asked to continue at growing intervals, up to an hour apart. Past this many hours without a working turn, Needs You gets a row. 0 = keep asking hourly for ever.

agentFarm.batonFlaggedPasses.description: When the engine flags a leg's conversation, nothing in that session is answered again, so the baton is passed for it through the same brakes as any pass and the flagged card is closed. This is how many such passes may come in a row before the chain waits for you in Needs You. 0 = no cap of its own; the leg ceiling still applies.

agentFarm.batonFlaggedModel.description: The model a successor opens on when the leg before it was also opened by a flagged pass; the engine advises a new session first, then another model. Empty = the chain keeps its own model.

agentFarm.chainHangMinutes.description: A relay chain is flagged as hanging when its running leg has been idle this long, or its session ended this long ago, without passing the baton or the chain being closed. Read from the record and the session, never from what the leg said. It shows on the Chains and Living pages and as a notice that withdraws itself once the chain moves.

agentFarm.chainWaitMinutes.description: A relay chain is flagged as stuck when its next leg has waited this long for the session that passed the baton to end. It shows on the Chains and Living pages and as a notice that withdraws itself once the next leg opens.

agentFarm.defaultAccountCeiling.description: The wall every unattended start obeys: an account at or past this share of its five-hour window is passed over; its week has Weekly account ceiling. Account policies, rule steps, relay legs and sentry rounds all obey it unless they name their own wall, and no wall acts above Quota handover at.

agentFarm.defaultAccountWeeklyCeiling.description: The same wall for the all-models week: an account at or past this share of its weekly window is passed over, while its five-hour window is judged by Account ceiling. Kept apart so an account past Account ceiling on its week is still used for days; the emptiest account still leads. It never acts above Weekly handover at.

agentFarm.contextHandoverStayAccountPct.description: When a run hands over for any reason but the quota and its account has used less than this share of its five-hour window, the next leg or sentry round opens on the same account, so one window is used up before another is started. It never acts above Account ceiling. 0 = off.

agentFarm.bridgeGuard.description: Stops an agent that searches the disk for a session's files by its id and has it ask Agent Farm, which knows where every session is. Only a real session id triggers it. Works on Claude and Codex; the other engines only have the rule in their instructions. A Console card shows an orange dot when a search was stopped.

agentFarm.shellGuard.description: Stops an agent's shell command that carries text the shell would silently damage (a non-ASCII letter, a backtick, a heredoc with backslashes, a long piece of inline text) and tells it to write the text to a file. Works on Claude and Codex; the other engines only have the rule in their instructions.

agentFarm.liveMonitor.description: Run the local live-event listener (127.0.0.1) that receives Claude Code hook events.

agentFarm.livePort.description: Port for the local live-event listener. Installed hooks follow a change by themselves.

agentFarm.stuckThresholdSeconds.description: How long a working session can go without events before it is marked stalled; its card says so, and with "Notify when a session stalls" on you also get a Needs You row and a notification. A session waiting on its own work (a purple wait, a command inside its time limit) is not stalled. 0 = never.

agentFarm.quotaStyle.percent.description: How a quota's percent is drawn on every page, as CSS declarations, e.g. color: #ff79c6; font-weight: 700. Empty = the default (purple, semibold). At 75% and 90% the page's own warning colours still win.

agentFarm.quotaStyle.left.description: How a quota's time left is drawn on every page, as CSS declarations, e.g. color: #89d185; font-weight: 700. Empty = the default (green, semibold).

agentFarm.quotaStyle.reset.description: How a quota's reset time is drawn on every page, as CSS declarations, e.g. color: #75beff; font-style: italic. Empty = the default (blue).

agentFarm.notifyPermission.description: Show a notification when an agent is waiting for a permission approval.

agentFarm.notifyStuck.description: When a session is marked stalled, give it a Needs You row and a notification. Off, only its card says stalled. Nothing to announce while "Stuck after" is 0.

agentFarm.notifyTurnEnd.description: Show a notification every time an agent finishes its turn.

agentFarm.permissionAnswerKeys.description: What Allow / Reject type into a session's terminal when you answer a permission prompt from Needs You; an empty field is the built-in. If the prompt does not move when you press Allow, put the key your CLI wants here. Escapes are literal: \u001b for ESC, \r for Enter.

allow.description: Allow this once. Default "1" — the first entry of the CLI's chooser.

allowAlways.description: Allow and stop asking for this. Default "2" — the second entry.

deny.description: Reject / cancel. Default ESC — the same key Interrupt sends, and the one answer here that is measured rather than reasoned.

agentFarm.alerts.on.description: Which events play their alert sound, for every session. These are sounds, separate from the VS Code notifications. Every event is off at first except Question card and Workflow asks you, where a person is waited on. A session set to Always still rings and one set to Silent never does (the ♪ on its Live Timeline row).

turn-ready.description: The turn finished and control is back with you.

question.description: The agent stopped to ask you something — a tool waiting for permission, or a question it needs answered. The turn is still open.

stalled.description: The session was working and has said nothing for longer than stuckThresholdSeconds.

error.description: A critical error. Nothing emits this edge yet; the voice is settable so it is ready when something does.

notice.description: A new notice on the Notices board that is not a question. Tied to no session.

notice-question.description: A question card on the Notices board: an agent waits for your answer, and some cards answer themselves when their time runs out. On out of the box.

gate.description: A workflow stopped to ask you something and waits for your answer. On out of the box.

quota.description: An account's five-hour window crossed the line the phone is warned at. Rings once per climb; falling back under it re-arms it. The name said is the account's.

mission.description: A mission ran to its end, done or failed. A mission you cancelled does not ring, and neither does a mission another mission started. The name said is the mission's title.

agentFarm.alerts.muted.description: Mute every alert sound across the whole farm: the 🔇 in the status bar, kept here so it survives a restart and every window sees it. Nothing is cleared, so unmuting brings your setup back. Sounds only; notifications keep working. One session can be muted on its own from its Live Timeline row.

agentFarm.alerts.toneVolume.description: How loud the alert tones play, 0–100; 100 is full volume. Every tone uses it: an event's, a reminder's, a run's own tone and Hear it. The announcement that says who has its own volume (Sound page › Voice). A player that cannot lower its level is used only as a last resort, at full volume.

agentFarm.alerts.reading.description: How an answer sounds when it is read aloud: a message's 🔊, Read Last Answer, Read Selection and Read aloud at the end of a turn. The announcement that says who has its own voice ("Say who"); a conversation's own voice still wins. Set on the Sound page › Voice › Reading.

voice.description: Empty means Auto: each reading is voiced by an installed voice of its own language — a Turkish answer by a Turkish voice, an English one by an English voice — and by the system voice where none is installed. A name, e.g. 'Microsoft Tolga', reads every text with that voice.

rate.description: Reading speed, −10 (slow) to 10 (fast); 0 is the voice's own normal. Separate from the announcement's speed — a long answer is often listened to faster.

enumDescriptions: Read aloud reads the first part of a long answer, stops at a sentence end and says there is more.
Read aloud reads the whole answer.
length.description: How much of an answer Read aloud reads when a turn ends. A reading you ask for always reads all of it.

enumDescriptions: A code block, an error trace, a log or JSON is said by its size, e.g. 'a 3-line code block'.
Code, traces, logs and JSON are left out without a word.
code.description: What a reading says where the answer has code, an error trace, a log or JSON.

agentFarm.alerts.quietHours.description: The hours the farm makes no sound in. The window wraps midnight: 23:00 to 08:00 is quiet from 23:00 through 07:59. A time that is not HH:MM leaves quiet hours off and says so on the card; a start equal to the end is an empty window, never all day. Sounds only, like the mute.

on.description: Whether the window is in force at all. Off out of the box.

from.description: When the quiet starts, HH:MM, local time. Inclusive.

to.description: When it ends, HH:MM, local time. Exclusive — at this minute sounds are back.

agentFarm.alerts.speak.description: Say which agent an alert is about, out loud, right after its tone: local and free (Windows System.Speech, macOS say, Linux spd-say), under the same mute and quiet hours. A sentence in your language needs a voice for it; on Windows this player sees only the SAPI 5 voices, so a language pack you installed may be missing from its list.

on.description: Off out of the box. A machine that talks unbidden is one people switch off entirely, taking the tones with it.

events.description: Which events are announced. Just 'question' by default: it is the one event where an agent is STOPPED and the cost of not knowing is the whole run standing still. A fleet that announces every finished turn out loud is one you silence in an afternoon — and then you hear nothing at all, including the question.

template.description: What is said. `{agent}`, `{event}` and `{session}` are substituted; everything else is spoken exactly as typed, so a mistyped `{agnet}` is HEARD rather than silently vanishing. Capped at 160 characters — every announcement holds the whole fleet's alerts for as long as it is speaking.

rate.description: Speaking rate, −10 (slow) to 10 (fast). 0 is the voice's own normal. On macOS this is mapped onto `say`'s words per minute for you.

volume.description: 0–100, the synthesiser's own volume. Separate from the tones, which are the OS mixer's.

voice.description: An installed voice by name, e.g. 'Microsoft Zira Desktop'. Empty means Auto: each announcement and reading is voiced by an installed voice of its own language, the system voice where none is installed. `alerts.speak` with no arguments lists what this player can select — the SAPI 5 set, which is not everything the machine has.

agentFarm.alerts.nudge.description: When an agent's question is still unanswered after the given minutes, a light tone reminds you, up to repeat times. Only questions: a finished turn needs nothing from you. It follows the mute and the quiet hours; minutes 0 switches it off.

minutes.description: Minutes of no answer before the first reminder. 0 = off. Clamped to 1–240.

repeat.description: How many reminders at most, after the alert itself. 0 = off. Clamped to 20.

voice.description: Which tone the reminder uses — deliberately its own, and lighter than the alert you already missed, because a second identical chime reads as a second question. Default: af_subtle_alert, the thinnest voice in the set. A tone this machine cannot play falls back to the event's own voice rather than going silent.

agentFarm.alerts.voices.description: Which sound each event plays; an empty one uses its built-in, and turn-ready and question differ so they can be told apart from another room. Twenty built-ins (ten af_… sounds and the earlier ten, kept for whoever chose one) plus your own (u-…). A sound whose file is missing falls through to the next answer and says so.

turn-ready.description: Voice for a finished turn. Default: af_crystal_turn — struck glass, a settled gesture that does not rise.

question.description: Voice for an agent asking you something. Default: af_intercom_knock — a knuckle on a panel, twice. Almost no pitch, so it is told apart from every chime by texture, which is what carries across a room.

stalled.description: Voice for a stalled session. Default: af_deep_sonar — a ping that falls while it rings, over a low body that outlasts it.

ended.description: Voice for a closed session. Default: af_marimba_success — wood, two notes up a fifth.

error.description: Voice for a critical error. Default: af_bell_urgent — three strikes that accelerate and rise. The tempo carries the urgency, so it does not have to be a buzzer people learn to hate and then switch off.

notice.description: Voice for a new notice that is not a question. Default: af_zen_chime — soft, for news nobody is waiting on.

notice-question.description: Voice for a question card on the Notices board. Default: af_pulse_start.

gate.description: Voice for a workflow asking you. Default: af_pop_advance.

quota.description: Voice for an account's quota running out. Default: af_subtle_alert.

mission.description: Voice for a mission that ended. Default: af_lullaby_sleep.

agentFarm.alerts.agentVoices.markdownDescription: Which sound each event plays for one agent's sessions: `{ "developer": { "question": "af_zen_chime" } }`. Above "Event sounds" and below a session's own choice. Easiest from the Sound page › Sessions › Agents.

agentFarm.taskExtraArgs.description: Extra command-line arguments added to a task's claude command, e.g. --model haiku to run routine work on a cheaper model. They are Claude Code flags, so a task on another engine (Codex, Gemini, Antigravity, OpenCode) ignores them; set that task's model and effort on the task itself.

agentFarm.externalTerminal.description: Open session terminals (Start, Continue, Resume) in the system terminal, Windows Terminal when there is one, instead of the one inside VS Code. It avoids drawing glitches (ghost spaces, lost lines) in long sessions. Farm tasks stay inside VS Code so their status can be followed. Also switched by Terminal Rendering Fix.

agentFarm.judgeArgs.description: CLI arguments for internal verification (judge) calls — keep this on a cheap model.

enumDescriptions: Hold the step and ask me whether to continue without a verdict.
Let it continue, marked NOT JUDGED in its output.
Stop the step as failed.
agentFarm.judgeUnjudged.description: When a quality gate cannot judge an asset — the judge cannot open a video or audio file, or it could not run — what happens. It is never counted as a pass.

enumDescriptions: When a media step edits an image or video it was given (a local file it uploaded, or an earlier step's result), its quality check sees that source too and judges only whether what was asked changed.
The quality check sees the result alone.
agentFarm.judgeCompare.description: Whether an edit's quality check is shown what it started from. Without it, a judge can take something already in the source for an unwanted addition and fail a correct edit.

agentFarm.kapici.rulesDir.description: Folder of your own Gatekeeper rules (one JSON file per rule). Empty = a _KAPICI folder inside every agent root. A project's .kapici folder is read too and wins over this one; the shipped rules come first.

agentFarm.kapici.timeoutMs.description: How long Gatekeeper waits for the classifier before handing the decision back to the usual path. A rule may set its own; the language-model judge, when used, waits at least a minute.

agentFarm.kapici.providers.description: Who Gatekeeper asks, in order, when a rule names no one: heuristic (local checks — numbers, dates, counts, patterns — never sent anywhere), jev (the small classifier; needs its key in the Secret vault), llm (the judge model — slower, costs a model call). A sensitive rule never goes to jev.

enumDescriptions: By the key found in the Secret vault: TYPESAFE_API_KEY goes to TypeSafe, AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY to the Vercel AI Gateway, OPENROUTER_API_KEY to OpenRouter. A named key goes by its name.
Straight to TypeSafe (api.typesafe.ai), model jev-1.13.0.
Through the Vercel AI Gateway (ai-gateway.vercel.sh), model typesafe-ai/jev — same questions, same answers. Vercel's free credit does not cover Jev.
Through OpenRouter's decisions endpoint (openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions), model typesafe/jev-1.13 — same questions, same answers, billed from the OpenRouter credit.
agentFarm.kapici.route.description: Which road Gatekeeper takes to the classifier.

agentFarm.kapici.keyName.description: The Secret vault name of the classifier's key. Empty = TYPESAFE_API_KEY, else AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, else OPENROUTER_API_KEY, whichever the vault holds. A name containing openrouter / vercel / gateway picks that road when the road is auto. Mark it Farm only on the Secrets page so no agent receives it.

enumDescriptions: Routing works exactly as it always has: your dispatch rules, then the classifier model if it is on.
Routing works exactly as it always has, and Gatekeeper quietly makes its own pick beside it and records whether the two agreed (see how often in the Gatekeeper audit). Nothing waits for it.
When no dispatch rule matches, Gatekeeper picks the agent first; when it is not sure, or cannot answer, the classifier model decides as before.
agentFarm.kapici.dispatch.description: Whether Gatekeeper helps decide which agent takes incoming work. Try shadow for a week or two before switching it on.

enumDescriptions: A held retry is decided exactly as it always has: the supervisor model your retry policy names, and its fallback when it cannot answer.
The supervisor model decides as it always has, and Gatekeeper quietly makes its own pick beside it and records whether the two agreed (see how often in the Gatekeeper audit). Nothing waits for it.

Gatekeeper decides first whether to resume, wait or stop; when it is not sure, or cannot answer, the supervisor model decides as before. A retry policy may also name Gatekeeper itself as its supervisor, which then asks no model at all.
agentFarm.kapici.retry.description: Whether Gatekeeper helps decide what happens to a task whose retry is held for a supervisor. Try shadow for a week or two before switching it on.

enumDescriptions: A trigger with a Gatekeeper precondition fires exactly as if it had none: its other brakes decide, as always.
Triggers fire as they always have, and Gatekeeper quietly says beside each firing whether it saw real work in it, recorded in the Gatekeeper audit. Nothing waits for it.

A trigger with a Gatekeeper precondition asks it last, after its cheaper brakes, and does not wake the agent when Gatekeeper is sure there is no work. When it is not sure, the trigger fires; when it cannot answer, the rule decides.
agentFarm.kapici.trigger.description: Whether Gatekeeper is asked before a trigger wakes an agent, so a change that is only noise (an auto-save, a lock file, a formatting-only edit) costs no run. Try Shadow for a week or two before switching it on.

enumDescriptions: A workflow's Gatekeeper step carries on as if it were not there; nothing is asked.
A Gatekeeper step carries on as always, and Gatekeeper quietly records beside it where it would have sent the run (see the Gatekeeper audit). Nothing waits for it.
A Gatekeeper step asks its rule and routes the run: carry on, stop, or ask you. When it is not sure or cannot answer, the rule decides — most rules carry on.
agentFarm.kapici.workflow.description: Whether a workflow's Gatekeeper steps are asked. A Gatekeeper step reads what the run has made so far and decides, without a model, whether the chain goes on. Try shadow for a week or two before switching it on.

enumDescriptions: Ask me before a file from this computer is sent to the provider.
Upload it and use its URL, without asking.
Never — the step fails and says which file; {upload:<path>} still uploads.
agentFarm.mediaUploadAuto.markdownDescription: A media step whose input names a file on this computer: fal and Replicate only read web addresses, so the file is uploaded to the provider's storage and its address sent instead. `{upload:<path>}` in the input always uploads. The same content is uploaded once.

enumDescriptions: The media step's own provider (a replicate: model uploads to Replicate, anything else to fal).
Always fal's storage.
Always Replicate's files.
agentFarm.mediaUploadProvider.description: Where a local file in a media input is uploaded.

agentFarm.mediaUploadRetentionDays.markdownDescription: How long fal keeps an uploaded file; after that it is uploaded again when a step needs it. 0 = fal's own default. Replicate sets its own expiry.

agentFarm.workflowPrevTextChars.markdownDescription: How much of the previous step's text a workflow step's `{prev_text}` carries. Any earlier step's whole text (up to 20,000 characters) is also readable as `{steps.<id>.text}`.

agentFarm.toolOutDir.markdownDescription: Where a tool step writes what an ffmpeg recipe makes. Empty = an af-tool folder beside the input. A step or a call can name its own.

enumDescriptions: An output already there refuses the step, saying which file.
An output already there gets a new name (-2, -3, …).
An output already there is replaced.
agentFarm.toolOverwrite.markdownDescription: What a tool step does when a file it would write is already there.

agentFarm.showrunner.markdownDescription: The agent that fills every role a workflow step names (writer, editor, publisher...) when the workflow binds that role to nobody. A workflow binds its roles on its form (Roles).

agentFarm.judgeLadder.markdownDescription: The models a workflow step's quality check uses, cheapest first (e.g. haiku,sonnet). The check runs on the first; a fail is judged once more on the next before the step is paid for again, and a pass there overturns it. A step naming its own judge keeps it. Empty = the one judge of Judge arguments. A run or a cost preset can set its own.

agentFarm.workflowSpendCap.markdownDescription: The most one workflow run may spend, in dollars, counting every step and supervisor turn. Once reached, no further step or branch starts and the run stops, saying so; nothing is asked. 0 = no cap. A workflow can set its own cap on its form (Run cap $), and one run can override both.

agentFarm.airtableInputStages.markdownDescription: Which stage folders an Airtable workflow input searches when it names none (source, raw, semi, final, asset).

agentFarm.airtableInputLimit.markdownDescription: At most this many records an Airtable workflow input hands a run.

enumDescriptions: Newest records first.
Oldest records first.
Alphabetically by name.
agentFarm.airtableInputSort.markdownDescription: The order an Airtable workflow input hands its records in.

agentFarm.studioLibraryBase.markdownDescription: Which local Airtable database the Studio wall reads its media records from. Empty = the Airtable page's default.

agentFarm.studioLibraryStages.markdownDescription: Which stage folders the Studio wall shows (source, raw, semi, final, asset). Empty = every stage.

enumDescriptions: Every kind.
Images only.
Videos only.
Audio only.
agentFarm.studioLibraryKind.markdownDescription: Which kind of media the Studio wall shows. Empty = every kind.

enumDescriptions: Both.
Only the files that passed.
Only the failed ones.
agentFarm.studioLibrarySuccess.markdownDescription: Which outcome the Studio wall shows: only the files that passed, only the failed ones, or empty = both.

enumDescriptions: Ask before a promotion moves the file and its record
Promote at once
agentFarm.studioLibraryPromote.markdownDescription: A promotion on the Studio wall (raw to asset, semi to final) moves the file into the next stage folder and its Airtable record with it. Ask first confirms; At once does not.

enumDescriptions: Leave it in all_in and ask on Notices
Leave it in all_in for the next pass, without a question
agentFarm.allInUnsure.markdownDescription: A file in the all_in waiting area that the model is not sure of, cannot open, or is not media stays where it is. Ask posts one Notices question listing them; wait leaves them for the next pass.

enumDescriptions: The manager's daily media batch processes all_in
Only a call by hand (bridge media.allin) processes it
agentFarm.allInWhen.markdownDescription: When a media library's all_in waiting area is processed, each file looked at by a model (about two turns a file: its stage, then its form). Daily: the manager's daily media batch runs it. By hand: only a call does.

enumDescriptions: When the run has ended — one pass over its final and failed files.
As soon as a file is in scope (filed final, failed, left out).
Never — only media.enrich fills a record.
agentFarm.libraryEnrich.markdownDescription: When a model looks at a run's recorded files and fills their record's meaning. A workflow's Library block can say otherwise.

enumDescriptions: The final output and the failed or left-out files (their salvage notes).
Only the final output.
Every recorded file, parts too — one model turn each.
agentFarm.libraryEnrichScope.markdownDescription: Which of a run's recorded files get their meaning filled.

agentFarm.libraryEnrichModel.markdownDescription: The Claude model that looks at an image to fill its record.

agentFarm.libraryEnrichVideoModel.markdownDescription: The Antigravity model that looks at a video to fill its record; it sees frames, not sound.

agentFarm.libraryEnrichEffort.markdownDescription: The claude effort for filling a record.

agentFarm.libraryEnrichSections.markdownDescription: Which record sections a model fills, comma separated: identity, taxonomy, function, tone, education, marketing, platform, accessibility, seo, tags, salvage. Empty = all.

agentFarm.libraryEnrichCap.markdownDescription: What one Claude turn may spend filling a record. 0 = no cap. A turn's own start costs about $0.02 (measured on haiku), so a cap under $0.05 stops every turn. Antigravity reports no cost, so it is not held there.

enumDescriptions: The mission's lead is asked first; a question it leaves open comes to you.
Only the lead is asked; a question it leaves open goes unanswered and the run carries on the mechanical way.
It comes straight to you, as a workflow you started yourself does.
agentFarm.workflowAskEscalation.markdownDescription: When a workflow a mission started asks a question at a checkpoint, who is asked. A workflow you started yourself always asks you. Whoever answered is written on the run's board, which the mission reads with the result.

agentFarm.taskRetry.markdownDescription: What happens when an unattended task fails, unless the run sets its own rule. Empty = six attempts, forty minutes apart, only when the session limit was hit, so the work never ran. The first three waits can be set one by one; later ones follow the strategy. With reset-aware on, a limit failure waits until the window reopens, plus the safety buffer.

max.description: How many times to try AGAIN after a failure. 0 = never retry.

delayMin.description: Minutes to wait before the first retry. It is also 'base' in the formula below.

delay2Min.description: Minutes before the SECOND retry. Leave it out and the strategy below decides that one too.

delay3Min.description: Minutes before the THIRD retry. Leave it out and the strategy below decides that one too.

enumDescriptions: Every retry waits the same number of minutes.
The wait doubles each time (capped at 12 hours) — the right shape against something that is busy rather than broken.
base × n — a gentler ramp than doubling.
Your own arithmetic, in 'formula' below.
backoff.description: How the wait grows for retry 4 and after. The first three can be stated one by one above.

formula.markdownDescription: The wait for retry 4 and after, in minutes, when `backoff` is `formula`. Variables: `n` (which retry this is), `prev` (the wait before it), `base` (`delayMin`). Operators `+ - * / ^`, brackets, `min(a,b)` and `max(a,b)`. Example: `min(prev * 1.5, 120)`. ‼️ It is PARSED, never evaluated as code — anything outside this grammar is refused with the reason.

capMin.description: The longest any computed wait may become, in minutes. The built-in 12-hour ceiling applies on top of it.

resetAware.description: When the failure really was a usage/session limit, wait for the WINDOW rather than for a number: the first retry goes at the reset time the engine published (or printed) plus the safety buffer below. Retries 2 and 3 use their own minutes and 4+ the strategy.

safetyBufferMin.description: Minutes to add to the stated reset time before the first retry goes (default 3). The window reopening and the CLI agreeing that it has are not the same instant.

enumDescriptions: Only when the Claude usage/session limit was hit, so nothing was attempted. This is the default.
Any non-zero exit.
when.description: Which failures are worth trying again.

prompt.description: Sent INSTEAD of the original prompt on a retry. Leave empty to send the same work again. A retry is a fresh headless run with no memory of the last one, so a prompt here has to stand on its own.

enumDescriptions: A retry is a FRESH run: the original prompt (or the one above) into a new conversation. The default, and what every policy written before this field means.
A retry after a run that had ALREADY DONE WORK is a CONTINUATION: wait for the window, resume that run's own session, and send the continuation prompt as the next turn.
`smart`, except that after a LIMIT cut off work the engine named in `supervisor` decides, read-only, how it goes on. Without `supervisor.engine` it is plain `smart`.
behavior.markdownDescription: ‼️ What a retry IS. `smart` decides between the two off what the failed run's own transcript proves it managed to do — it never guesses: a run that started nothing is retried normally, a run that was CUT OFF is resumed. A run whose transcript is not bound yet obeys `unknownProgressFallback`.

continuationPrompt.markdownDescription: The words sent when picking work back up (`behavior: smart`). It goes as the NEXT TURN of that run's own conversation, so it can be short — everything the run knew is still in front of it. Empty uses the built-in default ("carry on, read the transcript and the working folder first, do not redo finished work"). Placeholders: `{taskTitle}` `{attempt}` `{failureReason}` `{resetAt}` `{progressSummary}`; an unknown one is left in the text rather than blanked.

continuationPrompt2.description: The SECOND pick-up, when picking up twice needs different words from picking up once. Empty falls back to continuationPrompt.

continuationPromptLater.description: The third pick-up and every one after it. Empty falls back to continuationPrompt2, then continuationPrompt.

enumDescriptions: Create the retry and HOLD it visibly until the evidence lands, then remake it into the right shape. The default.
Treat it as an ordinary retry and send the original prompt.
Do not retry at all.
Hold it and put the question to you.
unknownProgressFallback.markdownDescription: ‼️ What `smart` does when nobody can yet say whether the failed run had done any work. The one thing that must not happen is the original prompt going out as if the run had been idle — which is why the default HOLDS rather than guessing.

supervisor.markdownDescription: Who decides how a run cut off by a LIMIT goes on when `behavior` is `supervisor`: it reads what the run left and answers resume · run the original again · wait · stop · ask you. It runs read-only and never commits, pushes or closes anything. Needs `engine`; the rest have defaults.

engine.description: The engine that judges — claude, codex, gemini, agy… An engine on the same plan as the task is asked only after the reset.

model.description: The model it judges with. Empty = the engine's default.

agent.description: The agent folder it runs in, read-only. Empty = the task's own agent.

maxCalls.description: How many times it may be asked per task, all limits together. Past it, the deterministic continuation is used.

budgetUsd.description: Dollars across all its calls for one task. 0 or empty = no money cap (the call cap still holds).

minConfidence.description: A decision it is less sure of than this is not applied; lowConfidence decides instead.

enumDescriptions: Continue deterministically, as smart would.
Hold the task and ask you.
Do not retry.
lowConfidence.description: What happens when its answer is below minConfidence, or it cannot be asked at all.

carryOn.markdownDescription: ‼️ At a LIMIT, which sign-in carries the work on. **Empty (the default) = stay**: the run keeps the account it was given and waits for that plan's reset. `@emptiest`, `@round-robin` or `@<one of your named rules>` lets that rule choose among the engine's OTHER captured accounts; a slot id (e.g. `claude-work`) names the one account to carry on with, if it has room. A run's own policy (Tasks form → Retry → *At a limit, carry on with*) overrides this.

agentFarm.maxConcurrentTasks.description: Maximum tasks running at once across the whole farm (0 = unlimited). Excess starts are deferred and launched automatically.

agentFarm.maxConcurrentPerAgent.description: Maximum tasks running at once per agent (0 = unlimited).

agentFarm.quotaGuardPercent.description: Hold automatic task starts once the five-hour window reaches this share of its limit (needs Window limit or Weighted window limit). 0 = off. Even at 0, a task naming an account whose own window is at or past the quota handover line waits for that window instead of starting only to hand over.

agentFarm.outputsMaxMB.description: Size cap for the archived task outputs folder; oldest unreferenced outputs are pruned (0 = unlimited).

agentFarm.mediaAuthSecret.description: The Secrets name of your fal.ai key; store it with Set Secret.

agentFarm.replicateAuthSecret.description: The Secrets name of your Replicate API token, used by media models with a replicate: prefix; store it with Set Secret.

agentFarm.replicateBaseUrl.description: Override the Replicate API base URL (testing / self-hosted proxy). Empty = https://api.replicate.com.

agentFarm.codexHome.description: Codex CLI home whose sessions/ rollout transcripts feed the external-session history. Empty = ~/.codex.

agentFarm.geminiDir.description: Gemini CLI tmp dir whose chat files feed the external-session history. Empty = ~/.gemini/tmp.

agentFarm.agentEngineDefaults.description: Each agent's default model and effort on engines with no settings file of their own, passed as --model / --effort at launch. Claude's goes in the agent's .claude/settings.local.json; a Claude row may name a provider route and tier instead. Edit it in Farm Settings › Agent folders, where each box says what Default resolves to.

agentFarm.agyHome.description: Antigravity CLI home whose conversation index feeds the external-session history. Its own transcripts are protobuf inside per-conversation SQLite files and are not read; the index gives the title, the time and the workspace. Empty = ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli.

agentFarm.opencodeHistory.description: Read OpenCode's conversations into the sessions tables. OpenCode publishes no transcript file, so its CLI is run for this, slowly and in the background. Turn it off and OpenCode conversations stop appearing; nothing is deleted.

agentFarm.mediaBaseUrl.description: Override the fal.ai queue base URL (testing / self-hosted proxy). Empty = https://queue.fal.run.

agentFarm.vaultDir.markdownDescription: Your notes vault, if you keep one. Other folder settings can be written from it as `${vault}/…`. Empty = no vault on this machine: a folder setting that uses `${vault}` is then skipped rather than pointed at a half-built path.

agentFarm.workArea.markdownDescription: The agents' scratch folder for drafts, test fixtures, logs and temporary scripts: an absolute folder, or a template such as `${temp}/agent_farm`. It is created when first needed and every session is told it. Change it and the old folder is retired: a write into it is refused.

enumDescriptions: Wait for a yes before anything is sent.
Publish without asking.
Rehearse: build and record the payload, send nothing.
agentFarm.publishApproval.markdownDescription: Before a publish step sends anything: Ask me waits for a yes, Publish sends without asking, Rehearse only builds and records the payload and sends nothing. A step's own approval wins.

agentFarm.publishPlatforms.markdownDescription: The platforms a publish step offers, in your order of priority (the first is the step card's default).

agentFarm.metricsFields.markdownDescription: Which numbers a metrics step asks your n8n flow for and the briefs show. Whatever the flow answers still lands on the media record. A step's own list wins.

agentFarm.performanceBrief.markdownDescription: Put how similar published content performed into the briefs: the {performance} placeholder of an idea or script step, and the workflow supervisor's brief. Off = both stay empty. The numbers come from the metrics step's last pull.

agentFarm.contentCalendarDir.markdownDescription: The content calendar: a vault folder with one note per publish, in the Full Calendar plugin's frontmatter plus platform, status, url, record and publishedAt; a publish step updates its note when it ends. Takes the path variables `${vault}`, `${workspace}` and `${home}`. Empty = `${vault}/01_INBOX/02_Calendar/CONTENT`.

agentFarm.reportDir.markdownDescription: Where agents' full reports are written, one file each (YYYY-MM-DD_<name>.md). Accepts `${vault}`, `${workspace}`, `${home}`, `${today}` and `${date:YYMMDD}`. Empty = `${vault}/00_AGENT_AREA/00_OUTPUT/10_REPORT`.

agentFarm.answerDir.markdownDescription: Folder where the detailed answer to a work queue item is written (not a report you asked for), named `YYYY-MM-DD_<agent>_<name>.md`. It takes the same path variables as Reports folder. Empty = `${vault}/00_AGENT_AREA/00_OUTPUT/01_CEVAPLAR`.

agentFarm.queue.targets.description: Targets (repos or areas) offered in the work queue's add form and filter, next to the agents' names. Free text; empty by default.

agentFarm.queue.groupSize.description: How many work queue items for one target are gathered before they are handed out as one. The manager may send a group sooner for its age or urgency.

agentFarm.queue.maxAgeHours.description: How long the oldest item in a work queue group may wait before the group is handed out anyway, however small, so nothing waits for ever.

label.description: source label shown in the gallery (default: folder name)

projectId.description: auto-assign ingested assets to this production id

sceneId.description: auto-assign to this scene id (needs projectId)

agentFarm.ingestFolders.description: Media ingest folders (downloads, render exports…): scanned every 30s; new image/video/audio files are registered into the Media Gallery in place (no copy). Files older than 48h at scan time are ignored.

agentFarm.mediaBudgetMonthUSD.description: Warn once per month when estimated media cost over the last 30 days exceeds this amount (USD). 0 = off.

agentFarm.mediaPricing.description: Estimated media pricing rules (USD): {match, usd, per: request|image|second}. Verify against fal.ai pricing.

match.description: Regular expression tested against the media model id. The first rule that matches wins, so put the narrow ones above the broad ones.

usd.description: Estimated price in USD for one unit of whatever `per` names.

per.description: What one unit is: a whole request, one produced image, or one second of video or audio.

agentFarm.notifyWebhookUrl.description: Forward farm notifications (permission, stalled, budget, workflow done/failed) to this webhook URL as JSON — e.g. an n8n webhook that relays to Telegram. Supports {secret:NAME}.

agentFarm.notifyWebhookEvents.description: Which notification types are posted to the webhook address.

agentFarm.dailyDigest.description: Send a compact fleet scorecard to the webhook after this local time each day (HH:MM, e.g. 21:30); off disables it. No model call. Send one by hand: Send Daily Digest Now.

match.description: A case-insensitive regex tested against the incoming text.

agent.description: The name of the agent that takes the work.

agentFarm.dispatchRules.description: Dispatcher routing rules for 'dispatch' triggers — first matching regex wins. Example: [{"match": "invoice|billing", "agent": "agent_one"}].

agentFarm.dispatchClassifier.description: When no dispatch rule matches, the model set in Judge arguments picks the agent from each CLAUDE.md.

enumDescriptions: No search by meaning.
Google's Gemini API; its key goes in Secrets.
Any OpenAI-compatible /embeddings endpoint, local ones included.
agentFarm.embeddingsProvider.description: Embeddings for search by meaning: Gemini (Google's API, key in Secrets) or OpenAI-compatible (any /embeddings endpoint, a local Ollama or LM Studio too, no key needed).

agentFarm.embeddingsModel.description: Embedding model id. Empty = provider default (gemini-embedding-001 / text-embedding-3-small; for Ollama e.g. nomic-embed-text).

agentFarm.embeddingsBaseUrl.description: Override the embeddings endpoint base URL. For local Ollama: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1

agentFarm.embeddingsSecret.description: Vault secret name holding the embeddings API key. Empty = GEMINI_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY by provider; local endpoints may need none.

agentFarm.semanticMaxSessions.description: How many most-recent sessions the semantic index covers.

agentFarm.searchToolTrailDays.description: How long after a session's last activity its tool trail (what each tool was asked and answered) stays in the text search index; only an Everything search reads it. After that the session keeps its dialogue and drops the trail, and an Everything search reaching it re-reads the transcript, slower. 0 keeps every trail.

agentFarm.browserAllowHosts.description: Global host allowlist for browser steps (subdomains included). A browser step refuses to run if neither this nor its own allowHosts covers the URL.

enumDescriptions: Confirm every browser step before it runs (recommended).
Run browser steps on allowed sites without asking.
agentFarm.browserApproval.description: Whether every browser step is confirmed before it runs (recommended), or steps on allowed sites run without asking.

name.description: profile name shown in the task wizard

headless.description: command template with {prompt} and {args}, e.g. gemini -p "{prompt}"

interactive.description: optional interactive template; falls back to headless

agentFarm.cliProfiles.description: Command lines a task can run for a CLI Agent Farm knows nothing else about. Such a task gets its output archived and its exit code, nothing more: no transcript, cost or live events. Codex, Gemini, Antigravity and OpenCode are engines of their own; pick one of those on the task instead.

file.description: path to the synced relay-*.jsonl written by farmRelay.js on that machine

agentFarm.relayFeeds.description: Live feeds from other machines: run farmRelay.js there (Save Relay Script for Another Machine…), sync its output file here, and list it in this setting.

agentFarm.packGalleryRepos.description: Agent pack gallery sources: git URLs (shallow-cloned into extension storage) or local folders containing .agentpack files.

agentFarm.digestTtsModel.description: The fal.ai text-to-speech model the spoken daily briefing is recorded with (check the exact id on fal.ai); the file goes to "Briefing audio folder" and is paid from your fal key. Empty: this computer reads the briefing aloud for free, with the Sound page's reading voice.

agentFarm.digestTtsFolder.description: Where the spoken briefing's audio is saved when "Briefing voice model" names a fal.ai model, e.g. a phone-synced folder. Empty = the automatic reports folder.

source.description: Which launches the rule applies to.

agent.description: A case-insensitive regex on the agent name; empty = any agent.

promptMatch.description: A case-insensitive regex on the prompt; empty = any prompt.

model.description: The model id or alias the task runs on (passed as --model).

agentFarm.modelPolicy.description: Rule-based model routing for farm-launched tasks; first match wins. Example: [{"source": "trigger", "model": "haiku"}] runs all trigger-born work on a cheap model.

name.description: what the rule is picked by; referred to as @<name>. Letters, digits, _ and - only, and never a built-in's name.

note.description: one line for the picker's panel, under what the rule currently comes to

engine.description: when set, the rule is for one engine and refuses a launch on another (an account belongs to one engine, so a rule does too)

ceiling.description: the wall, as a percentage of the window, for every step that names none (default the Account ceiling, agentFarm.defaultAccountCeiling). A rule's or a step's own wall never acts above agentFarm.quotaHandoverPct — a session STARTED past the handover line is told to hand over on its first reading

enumDescriptions: walk the steps top to bottom; the first with a usable answer wins, so step 1 carries every launch until it is walled
the listed accounts are a pool of their own: whichever has the most room RIGHT NOW starts. Every step must then be an account — a rule has no single figure to compare
strategy.description: how the steps are read (default chain)

chain.description: the steps. chain: walked top to bottom, the first with a usable answer wins; emptiest: compared, the one with the most room wins. A step names an account OR a policy, never both.

policy.description: a built-in (@emptiest, @pool, @standing, @round-robin) or another named rule (@<name>)

ceiling.description: this step's own wall; the rule's, then the default, otherwise

models.description: taken only when the launch's model is one of these (empty/absent = any)

agentFarm.accountPolicies.markdownDescription: **Named rules for which sign-in a launch runs on**, offered in every account picker beside `@emptiest`, `@pool`, `@standing` and `@round-robin`, decided at each launch. A rule that can choose nothing refuses the launch and says why. Example: `[{"name": "Night", "chain": [{"account": "spare"}, {"policy": "@emptiest", "ceiling": 80}]}]` is `@Night`.

agentFarm.quotaDowngradePercent.description: When the five-hour window reaches this share of its limit, tasks the farm launches run on Downgrade model. 0 = off.

agentFarm.quotaDowngradeModel.description: Model forced when the quota downgrade kicks in.

agentFarm.permissionLint.description: Audit each agent's permission rules (blanket allows, dangerous patterns, unused broad rules) and surface findings in Insights.

agentFarm.pulse.description: A fixed cheap prompt per agent, judged by a cheap model for whether the answer matches the agent's identity; a small API cost per agent. Run one by hand with Run Pulse Check Now.
